Does this new plan remember the old discussion: "  # External LES Inspiration Plan

  ## Summary

  Use Coq-HoTT and Buchholtz-Rijke as architectural guides for escaping the current normalization trap. The main
  shift is to avoid proving ordinary group exactness by repeatedly expanding concrete homotopy-group wrappers.
  Instead, introduce a lower-level exactness notion whose core datum is the map into the fiber/kernel, then derive
  the group-facing statement only at fixed Hopf indices.

  ## Key Sources

  - Coq-HoTT ExactSequence.v: useful because it defines exactness through a complex-induced map into a fiber and
    connectedness of that map, then proves loop/truncation preservation before packaging LES consumers. This
    suggests replacing our current image/kernel transport-first approach with a “map-to-fiber first” bridge.

  - Buchholtz-Rijke LES of homotopy n-groups: directly relevant conceptually; it proves that fiber sequences induce
    exactness after truncation and frames the result at the n-group level, which matches the shape we need better
    than ordinary group image/kernel transport. (arxiv.org (https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.08696?utm_source=openai))

  - Coq-HoTT library generally: a credible source of synthetic homotopy proof architecture, but not a code-port
    target because its typeclass/modality machinery differs from agda-unimath.

  - Cubical Agda Brunerie work: useful later for large synthetic homotopy decomposition and performance discipline,
    but less directly useful for the current LES bridge obstruction. (arxiv.org
    (https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.00151?utm_source=openai))

  ## Implementation Changes

  - Add a small intermediate exactness bridge below group-exactness-from-set-truncated-homotopy-group-exactness:
      - Define a local “set-level exactness as fiber/preimage” lemma for pointed sets.
      - Prove that the existing set-truncated LES exactness gives this fiber/preimage form without mentioning
        Concrete-Group.

      - Only then translate the fiber/preimage result to ordinary group image/kernel exactness.

  - Avoid generic named homotopy-group wrapper proofs.
      - Pass coherence squares explicitly.
      - Instantiate at fixed maps/indices only after the lower-level lemma checks.

  - Treat Coq-HoTT’s exactness transfer lemmas as a checklist:
      - exactness preserved by homotopy of either map,
      - exactness transferred across equivalences/squares,
      - loop spaces preserve the exactness notion,
      - truncation converts fiber-sequence exactness to pointed-set exactness.

  ## Test Plan

  - First check only the new lower-level pointed-set/fiber-preimage module.
  - Then check group-exactness-from-set-truncated-homotopy-group-exactness.
  - Then check exactness-homotopy-groups-fiber-sequences and the Hopf LES consumer.
  - Use rg -n "\\{!!\\}|allow-unsolved-metas|postulate" after each milestone.

  ## Assumptions

  - We should not pursue the direct generic group image/kernel transport proof again.
  - Coq-HoTT is used for decomposition and lemma order only.
  - The immediate target remains the LES bridge, not Hopf or Freudenthal."
